newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Zedillo calls on Singaporeans to invest in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo calls on Singaporeans to invest in Mexico.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Wednesday called on Singaporean businessmen to invest in his country, saying the economic crisis which wracked Mexico in 1995 is now over.
"There is a world of opportunity to participate in an economy that will grow enormously in the years to come," Zedillo said in a speech to top Singaporean businessmen.
The current account deficit has been brought under control and unemployment had been cut to 5.2 percent by the end of September 1996 from 7.6 percent in August 1995, he said.
"Today, we are poised for solid economic growth," Zedillo said. "The Mexican economy has started to grow again."
Goh Chee Wee, Singapore's minister of state for trade and industry, said Zedillo's visit will "provide a fresh impetus for advancing the investment flows between Mexico and Singapore".

In 1995, Mexico suffered its worst recession in half a century. A devaluation of the peso in December 1994 triggered the crisis which caused more than a million people to lose their jobs. Soaring interest rates drove millions more into debt.
A Mexican official said Singapore firms would invest up to US$100 million in a variety of projects in Mexico in the years to come.
That amount includes a $50 million investment by Flextronics Pte Ltd to manufacture printed computer circuit boards in Guadalajara.
Natsteel Electronics Pte Ltd will invest $10.9 million to also build computer circuit boards in the same Mexican city.

Sei Woo Rubber Works, which produces rubber parts for pagers and appliances, said it will invest $3.6 million for a plant in Mexico. "The Singapore market is small," Y.K. Low, executive chairman of Sei Woo, told reporters in a briefing.
"Mexico is our gateway to the United States, Latin America and Canada," he said.
Zedillo held talks on Wednesday with Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.

The Mexican leader arrived on Tuesday and will leave on Thursday for South Korea. He visited China last week and went on to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Subic Bay in the Philippines.
